learn.hook: Who makes you laugh at home? Who tells you stories? Your family is your first team!
points: A family is a group of people who live together, love and care for each other.
Some families are small, with parents and children. Some are big, with grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins too.
A family where grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together under one roof is called a joint family.
Family members share work at home, like cooking, cleaning, shopping and caring for the old and the young.
Every family is different, and every family is special.

example.q: Think it through: Dadi has a bad knee and cannot climb stairs. How can the family help her?
steps: Dadi needs things from the upper floor.
Children can fetch things for her.
Parents can take her to the doctor.
When everyone helps a little, Dadi feels cared for.
example.answer: Each member helps in a small way, so the whole family takes care of Dadi.

learn.reallife: When you set the plates before dinner or water the plants, you are sharing family work.

games.title: Small family or joint family?
items: Mother, father and two children
Grandparents, parents, uncle, aunt and cousins
Mother and her daughter
Three brothers, their wives and children with grandparents
Father, mother and one son
Dada, Dadi, Chacha, Chachi, parents and kids

games.title: True or false?
items: All families have the same number of members.
Families can be small or big. The number of members is different in each family.
Sharing housework is a way of caring for the family.
When everyone helps, no one person gets too tired.
Children can help at home in small ways.
Children can fold clothes, water plants or set the table.
In a joint family, grandparents, uncles and aunts may live together.
A joint family has many relatives living under one roof.
Only grown-ups belong to a family.
Children, babies and old people are all members of a family.

quiz.q: Aman lives with his parents, his grandparents, his uncle, aunt and two cousins. What kind of family is this?
quiz.explain: Many relatives like grandparents, uncles and aunts living together make a joint family.
steps: Aman lives with grandparents, uncle, aunt and cousins too.
Many relatives living together under one roof make a joint family.
Answer: A joint family
quiz.mistake: Thinks a family with many members is still a small family

quiz.q: Which of these is a good way for a child to help at home?
options: Leaving toys all over the floor
quiz.explain: Folding dry clothes is a small job that helps the whole family.
steps: Family members share work at home.
Folding dry clothes is a small job that helps everyone.
The other choices make more work or trouble.
Answer: Folding the dry clothes
quiz.mistake: Does not link helping at home with sharing family work

quiz.q: What makes a group of people a family?
options: They all wear the same colour
They all go to the same school
They live together and care for each other
They all like the same food
quiz.explain: A family is about living together, love and care, not about looks or likes.
steps: A family is people who live together and care for each other.
Colours, school or food do not make a family.
Answer: They live together and care for each other
quiz.mistake: Thinks families are decided by looks or likes

quiz.q: Meera lives with her mother, her father and her baby brother. How many people are in her family, counting Meera?
quiz.explain: Mother, father, baby brother and Meera make 4 people.
steps: Mother, father, brother = 3
Add Meera: 3 + 1 = 4
Answer: 4
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count Meera herself

quiz.q: Nanaji cannot read small letters well. How can Riya help him?
options: Read the newspaper aloud to him
quiz.explain: Reading aloud is a kind way to help an older family member.
steps: Nanaji cannot read small letters.
Reading the newspaper aloud to him is a kind way to help.
Answer: Read the newspaper aloud to him
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the needs of older family members

quiz.q: Why do family members share housework?
options: So that one person does all the work
So that work gets done and no one is too tired
So that no one has to eat
So that the house gets messy
quiz.explain: When work is shared, it gets done quickly and everyone gets time to rest and play.
steps: When work is shared, it gets done quickly.
No one person gets too tired.
Answer: So that work gets done and no one is too tired
quiz.mistake: Thinks housework is only one person's job

quiz.q: Which of these is true about families?
options: Every family is exactly the same
Families can be different, but each one is special
quiz.explain: Families come in many sizes and kinds. Each family is special in its own way.
steps: Families can be small or big, and every family is different.
Every family is special in its own way.
Answer: Families can be different, but each one is special
quiz.mistake: Thinks one kind of family is better than another

quiz.q: Kabir's mother is unwell. Which is the kindest thing Kabir can do?
options: Ask her to cook his favourite dish
Bring her a glass of water and let her rest
quiz.explain: Bringing water and letting her rest shows care for a sick family member.
steps: A sick person needs care and rest.
Bringing water and letting her rest shows care.
Answer: Bring her a glass of water and let her rest
quiz.mistake: Thinks only of own wishes instead of the family member's needs

teach.ask: Gappu lives alone in a nest. What is a family, and how do family members help each other?
teach.praise: Lovely! A family lives together, cares for each other and shares the work. Gappu wants a family too!
teach.nudge: What do family members do for each other at home?

revise.summary: A family is people who live together, love and care for each other. Families can be small or joint, members share housework and care for the old and young, and every family is special.
focus: Caring for old and sick family members
remember: Joint family: grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins under one roof
Family members share cooking, cleaning, shopping and caring
Every family is different and special
traps: A family is not about wearing the same colour or liking the same food; it is about love and care.
Don't think only big or only small families are happy.

learn.hook: Who brings your letters? Who fixes a leaking tap? Lots of people help us every day!
points: A community is a group of families who live in the same area, like a village, a colony or a town.
People in a community help each other and celebrate festivals and fairs together.
Community helpers do work that everyone needs: farmers, doctors, nurses, teachers, postal workers and sanitation workers.
Electricians fix wires, plumbers fix pipes and taps, and carpenters make things from wood.
We should thank and respect every helper, because every job is important.

example.q: Think it through: The water pipe in your colony bursts. Whom do the families call, and why?
steps: Water is spilling and the taps are dry.
A plumber knows how to fix pipes.
The plumber mends the pipe.
Water comes back to every home.
example.answer: They call a plumber, because a plumber fixes water pipes and taps.

learn.reallife: When neighbours share sweets at festivals or clean the park together, the community grows stronger.

games.title: Match the helper to the work
pairs: Collects garbage and keeps streets clean

items.text: A ___ treats sick people in a hospital.
A ___ stitches clothes.
A ___ mends shoes and slippers.
A ___ makes tables and chairs from wood.

quiz.q: What is a community?
options: A group of families living in the same area
Only the people in one house
quiz.explain: A community is made of many families living in one place, like a village or colony.
steps: A community is a group of families.
They live in the same area, like a village or colony.
Answer: A group of families living in the same area
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a community with a single family

quiz.q: The fan in your classroom stops working because of a loose wire. Who should fix it?
quiz.explain: An electrician knows how to fix wires, switches and fans safely.
steps: The problem is a loose wire in a fan.
Electricians fix wires; plumbers fix pipes.
Answer: An electrician
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the work of a plumber and an electrician

quiz.q: Who keeps our streets clean by collecting garbage?
quiz.explain: Sanitation workers collect garbage and keep our area clean and healthy.
steps: Garbage must be collected to keep streets clean.
Sanitation workers do this job.
Answer: Sanitation workers
quiz.mistake: Does not know the work of sanitation workers

quiz.q: In Riya's village, everyone gathers to celebrate the harvest festival. This shows that people in a community…
options: come together and share happy times
quiz.explain: Celebrating together brings people of a community closer.
steps: People in a community celebrate festivals together.
Gathering for the harvest festival shows this.
Answer: come together and share happy times
quiz.mistake: Thinks community members live separately and never share

quiz.q: Which helper grows the rice and wheat that we eat?
quiz.explain: Farmers grow food crops like rice, wheat and vegetables.
steps: Farmers grow food crops like rice and wheat.
Answer: A farmer
quiz.mistake: Thinks food comes from shops without anyone growing it

quiz.q: Why should we respect every community helper?
options: Because every job is important for the community
quiz.explain: We need all kinds of work, so every helper and every job deserves respect.
steps: Every helper does work that everyone needs.
So every job is important.
Answer: Because every job is important for the community
quiz.mistake: Thinks some jobs are less important than others

quiz.q: Pooja's slipper strap breaks. Who can mend it?
quiz.explain: A cobbler mends shoes, slippers and bags.
steps: A broken slipper strap needs mending.
A cobbler mends shoes, slippers and bags.
Answer: A cobbler
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the cobbler with other helpers

quiz.q: Which is a good way to help your community?
options: Wasting water from the public tap
Helping clean the park with neighbours
quiz.explain: Cleaning the park together keeps a shared place nice for everyone.
steps: Public places are shared by everyone.
Cleaning the park together keeps it nice.
The other choices damage or dirty shared things.
Answer: Helping clean the park with neighbours
quiz.mistake: Does not see shared places as everyone's responsibility

teach.ask: Gappu is new in town! What is a community, and who are the helpers in it?
teach.praise: Super! A community is many families living in one place, and helpers like doctors and farmers do work we all need.
teach.nudge: Who are the people who help everyone in a village or town?

revise.summary: A community is a group of families living in the same area. People help each other and celebrate together, and community helpers do work everyone needs.
remember: Electrician: wires and fans; plumber: pipes and taps; carpenter: wood
Cobbler mends shoes; sanitation workers collect garbage
Farmers grow food; doctors and nurses treat the sick
Every job is important
traps: Don't call a plumber for a wire problem; call an electrician.
No job is less important than another.

learn.hook: Your breakfast roti needed a farmer, a miller, a shopkeeper and a cook. Wow!
points: To depend means to need someone or something. Depending on each other is called interdependence.
People depend on each other: the farmer grows grain, the shopkeeper sells it and we buy it.
Animals depend on plants for food, shelter and air to breathe. Birds build nests in trees.
Plants also depend on animals: bees and butterflies carry pollen between flowers, and birds spread seeds.
Plants give out oxygen, which we breathe in. We breathe out carbon dioxide, which plants use to make food.

example.q: Think it through: If all the bees in a mango orchard disappeared, what might happen to the mangoes?
steps: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.
Flowers need pollen to make fruits.
Without bees, fewer flowers get pollen.
So fewer mangoes grow.
example.answer: Fewer mangoes would grow, because plants depend on bees to carry pollen.

learn.reallife: Next time you eat a banana, think of the farmer, the truck driver and the fruit seller who brought it to you.

games.title: From field to plate
games.prompt: Put the journey of wheat in order
items: A farmer grows wheat in the field
The wheat is harvested
A mill grinds the wheat into atta
A shopkeeper sells the atta
Someone at home makes rotis

games.title: Who depends on whom?
pairs: Builds its nest in a tree

quiz.q: What does interdependence mean?
quiz.explain: Interdependence means people, plants and animals need each other.
steps: To depend means to need someone or something.
Depending on each other is interdependence.
Answer: Needing and helping each other
quiz.mistake: Thinks depending means doing everything alone

quiz.q: How do bees help plants?
options: They carry pollen from flower to flower
quiz.explain: When bees visit flowers for nectar, pollen sticks to them and goes to other flowers. This helps fruits form.
steps: Bees visit flowers for nectar.
Pollen sticks to them and is carried to other flowers.
Answer: They carry pollen from flower to flower
quiz.mistake: Thinks bees only take from plants and give nothing back

quiz.q: Which gas do plants give out that we breathe in?
quiz.explain: Green plants give out oxygen. We need oxygen to breathe.
steps: Plants give out oxygen; we breathe out carbon dioxide.
We breathe in oxygen.
Answer: Oxygen
quiz.mistake: Mixes up oxygen with carbon dioxide

quiz.q: A koel eats a ripe fruit and later drops the seed far away. A new plant grows there. How did the bird help?
quiz.explain: Birds that eat fruits drop seeds in new places, so new plants grow.
steps: The koel ate the fruit and dropped the seed far away.
A new plant grew there, so the bird helped the plant.
Answer: It spread the seed
quiz.mistake: Does not see that animals help plants spread

quiz.q: Which of these shows people depending on each other?
options: A tailor stitching a shirt for a farmer, who grows food for the tailor
quiz.explain: The tailor and the farmer each do work the other needs. That is interdependence.
steps: Interdependence: each does work the other needs.
The tailor stitches for the farmer; the farmer grows food for the tailor.
Answer: A tailor stitching a shirt for a farmer, who grows food for the tailor
quiz.mistake: Picks an action that involves only one person or thing

quiz.q: In the chain grass → deer → tiger, what does the deer depend on for food?
quiz.explain: The arrow shows who is eaten by whom. The deer eats grass.
steps: In grass → deer → tiger, the arrow points to the eater.
The deer eats grass.
Answer: Grass
quiz.mistake: Reads the arrows the wrong way round

quiz.q: How does a farmer use cow dung?
quiz.explain: Cow dung is a natural manure. It makes the soil rich so crops grow well.
steps: Cow dung is a natural manure.
It makes the soil rich so crops grow well.
Answer: As manure for the fields
quiz.mistake: Does not know that animal waste can help plants grow

quiz.q: If there were no trees near a village, which of these would be hardest for birds?
quiz.explain: Many birds build nests in trees. Without trees they lose their homes.
steps: Animals depend on plants for shelter.
Many birds build nests in trees.
Without trees, birds lose their homes.
Answer: Finding places to build nests
quiz.mistake: Does not link trees with shelter for animals

teach.ask: Gappu thinks he does not need anyone. Can you explain why we all depend on each other?
teach.praise: Wonderful! People, plants and animals all need each other. Even Gappu needs trees for his nest!
teach.nudge: What do plants give us? And how do animals help plants?

revise.summary: Interdependence means needing and helping each other. People depend on each other, animals depend on plants, and plants depend on animals for pollen and seed spreading.
focus: How people depend on each other
How plants and animals help each other
remember: Bees and butterflies carry pollen; birds spread seeds
Animals get food, shelter and air from plants
Plants give out oxygen; we breathe out carbon dioxide, which plants use
Cow dung is used as manure
traps: Plants give out oxygen, not carbon dioxide, for us to breathe.
In grass → deer → tiger, the deer eats grass, not the tiger.

learn.hook: Take a walk around your street. How many useful places can you spot?
points: The area around our home is our neighbourhood.
A neighbourhood has many useful places: a school, a market, a hospital, a post office, a bank, a park and a police station.
Each place meets a need. We buy vegetables at the market and post letters at the post office.
Public places like parks, roads and libraries belong to everyone, so we must keep them clean.
In an emergency in India, we can call 112 for help.

example.q: Think it through: Neha wants to borrow a storybook for free. Which place in her neighbourhood should she visit?
steps: She wants to borrow, not buy.
A shop sells books, so she would have to pay.
A library lends books to read and return.
example.answer: The library.

learn.reallife: Draw your own walk from home to school and mark every useful place you pass.

games.title: Match the place to its use
True or false?
items: A park is a public place that everyone can use.
Parks belong to the whole community.
We should throw wrappers on the road if there is no dustbin nearby.
We should keep the wrapper and throw it in a dustbin later.
A post office helps us send letters and parcels.
Postal workers carry letters and parcels to many places.
112 is a number we can call for help in an emergency in India.
112 is India's emergency helpline number.
A bank is the place to buy vegetables.
We buy vegetables at a market or a shop. A bank keeps money safe.

quiz.q: Where would you go to send a rakhi to your cousin in another city?
quiz.explain: The post office sends letters and parcels to other places.
steps: A rakhi must be sent to another city.
The post office sends letters and parcels.
Answer: Post office
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a post office does

quiz.q: Arjun has a high fever. Which place should his family take him to?
quiz.explain: Doctors and nurses at a hospital or clinic treat sick people.
steps: Arjun is sick with fever.
Doctors and nurses at a hospital or clinic treat sick people.
Answer: Hospital or clinic
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the uses of different places

quiz.q: What is a neighbourhood?
quiz.explain: The streets, shops and places near our home make up our neighbourhood.
steps: A neighbourhood is the area around our home.
Answer: The area around our home
quiz.mistake: Thinks neighbourhood means only one's house

quiz.q: Which number can you call for help in an emergency anywhere in India?
quiz.explain: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance help.
steps: India has one emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.
That number is 112.
Answer: 112
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the digits of the emergency number

quiz.q: Which of these is a public place?
quiz.explain: A public park is shared by everyone in the community.
steps: Public places belong to everyone.
A public park is shared; kitchens, bedrooms and bags are private.
Answer: A public park
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the difference between private and public places

quiz.q: Where do people keep their savings safe?
quiz.explain: A bank keeps our money safe and helps us save.
steps: A bank keeps our money safe and helps us save.
Answer: In a bank
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a bank is for

quiz.q: A house is on fire! Which helpers rush to put it out?
quiz.explain: Firefighters from the fire station come with water and put out fires.
steps: Firefighters from the fire station put out fires.
Answer: Firefighters
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of firefighters

quiz.q: Why should we keep public places clean?
options: Because they belong to no one
Because only the mayor uses them
Because they belong to everyone and we all use them
quiz.explain: Public places are shared, so keeping them clean is everyone's job.
steps: Public places are shared by all of us.
So keeping them clean is everyone's job.
Answer: Because they belong to everyone and we all use them
quiz.mistake: Thinks public places are nobody's responsibility

teach.ask: Gappu flew into a new neighbourhood. What places will he find there, and what are they for?
teach.praise: Great tour! Each place meets a need, and we keep public places clean for everyone.
teach.nudge: Name a place in a neighbourhood and say what it is used for.

revise.summary: Our neighbourhood is the area around our home, with useful places like a school, market, hospital, post office, bank, park and police station. Public places belong to everyone, and 112 is India's emergency number.
focus: Matching each place to the need it meets
Public places and keeping them clean
remember: Post office: letters and parcels; bank: keeps savings safe
Hospital: treats the sick; fire station: firefighters
Library: borrow books
112 = emergency number in India
traps: Public places belong to everyone, not to no one.
Don't go to a bank to post a letter; use the post office.

learn.hook: The sun can be your guide! Where does it come up in the morning?
points: There are four main directions: North, East, South and West.
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
If you face North, East is on your right, West is on your left and South is behind you.
Between the main directions are North-East, South-East, South-West and North-West.
A compass has a needle that points North. Travellers and sailors use it to find their way.

example.q: Think it through: Ravi faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on his left?
steps: The sun rises in the East, so Ravi faces East.
When you face East, North is on your left.
South is on your right and West is behind.
example.answer: North is on his left.

learn.reallife: Stand in your courtyard in the morning, face the sun and point out all four directions.

games.title: Directions in a circle
games.prompt: Start at North and go clockwise
items: North
East
South
West

items.text: The sun rises in the ___.
The sun sets in the ___.
The direction opposite to North is ___.
A compass needle points to the ___.
The direction between North and East is ___.

quiz.q: How many main directions are there?
quiz.explain: The four main directions are North, East, South and West.
steps: The main directions are North, East, South and West.
That is 4 directions.
Answer: 4
quiz.mistake: Counts the in-between directions as main directions

quiz.q: In which direction does the sun set?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
steps: The sun rises in the East.
It sets in the West.
Answer: West
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sunrise and sunset directions

quiz.q: Sita faces North. What is on her right?
quiz.explain: When you face North, East is on your right hand side.
steps: Facing North: East is on the right, West on the left.
Answer: East
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right

quiz.q: Which direction is opposite to East?
quiz.explain: East and West are opposite each other.
steps: East and West are opposite each other.
Answer: West
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opposite direction is the next one on the circle

quiz.q: Which tool has a needle that always points North?
quiz.explain: A compass needle turns and settles pointing North, so we can find all directions.
steps: A compass needle settles pointing North.
Answer: A compass
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a compass with other measuring tools

quiz.q: Arjun faces West. What is behind him?
quiz.explain: The direction behind you is opposite to the one you face. Opposite of West is East.
steps: The direction behind you is opposite the one you face.
Opposite of West is East.
Answer: East
quiz.mistake: Picks a side direction instead of the opposite one

quiz.q: What is the direction between South and West called?
quiz.explain: The direction between South and West is South-West.
steps: Between the main directions are NE, SE, SW and NW.
Between South and West is South-West.
Answer: South-West
quiz.mistake: Joins the wrong pair of main directions

quiz.q: Meena faces South. Which direction is on her left?
quiz.explain: Facing South, your left hand points East and your right hand points West.
steps: Facing South, your right hand points West.
Your left hand points East.
Answer: East
quiz.mistake: Uses the North-facing rule even when facing South

teach.ask: Gappu is lost! How can he find East, West, North and South?
teach.praise: Hooray! The sun rises in the East and sets in the West, and a compass points North. Gappu can find his way!
teach.nudge: Where does the sun rise and set? That can help Gappu.

revise.summary: There are four main directions: North, East, South and West, with North-East, South-East, South-West and North-West between them. The sun rises in the East and sets in the West, and a compass needle points North.
focus: The four main and four in-between directions
Finding left, right and behind when facing a direction
Using the sun and a compass
remember: Sun rises in the East, sets in the West
Facing North: East on the right, West on the left, South behind
Opposites: North–South, East–West
Compass needle points North
traps: Facing South, East is on your left, not your right.
Don't mix up South-West and North-West.

learn.hook: A map is like a bird's photo of your town, taken from high above!
points: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above.
Maps use small pictures called symbols to show things like schools, roads, trees and rivers.
The key (or legend) of a map tells us what each symbol means.
On most maps, North is at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right and West on the left.
A map is much smaller than the real place, but it shows where things are.

example.q: Think it through: On a map, the school is at the top and the park is at the bottom. Where is the park from the school?
steps: On a map, the top is North and the bottom is South.
The park is below the school.
So the park is to the South of the school.
example.answer: The park is South of the school.

learn.reallife: Ask an adult to show you a map on a phone or in an atlas. Find the arrow or letter N that shows North.

games.title: Map facts
items: A map shows a place as seen from above.
Maps are drawn as if you are looking down from the sky.
The key of a map tells us what the symbols mean.
The key, also called the legend, explains each symbol.
A map is always the same size as the real place.
A map is a much smaller drawing of a real place.
On most maps, East is on the left side.
On most maps, East is on the right and West is on the left.

quiz.q: What is a map?
options: A drawing of a place as seen from above
quiz.explain: A map shows a place from above, as a bird would see it.
steps: A map is a drawing of a place.
It shows the place as seen from above.
Answer: A drawing of a place as seen from above
quiz.mistake: Thinks a map is any picture

quiz.q: What does the key of a map tell us?
quiz.explain: The map key, or legend, explains the symbols used on the map.
steps: Maps use symbols.
The key (legend) tells what each symbol means.
Answer: What each symbol means
quiz.mistake: Takes the word 'key' to mean a door key

quiz.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
quiz.explain: Most maps are drawn with North at the top.
steps: Most maps are drawn with North at the top.
Answer: North
quiz.mistake: Does not know the usual layout of a map

quiz.q: On a map with North at the top, the temple is on the right of the pond. In which direction is the temple from the pond?
quiz.explain: On a map with North at the top, the right side is East.
steps: On most maps, East is on the right.
The temple is on the right of the pond.
Answer: East
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the East and West sides of a map

quiz.q: Why do maps use symbols?
options: To show many things clearly in a small space
To make maps harder to read
Because symbols are bigger than words
quiz.explain: Symbols are small, simple pictures, so many things fit clearly on one map.
steps: Symbols are small, simple pictures.
Many things fit clearly in a small space.
Answer: To show many things clearly in a small space
quiz.mistake: Does not see why maps need symbols

quiz.q: On a map with North at the top, the market is at the bottom and the bus stand is at the top. Where is the market from the bus stand?
quiz.explain: The bottom of a map is South, so the market is South of the bus stand.
steps: On most maps, the bottom is South.
The market is at the bottom, below the bus stand.
Answer: South
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the top and bottom of a map

quiz.q: A blue wavy line on a map most likely shows…
quiz.explain: Maps usually show rivers with blue wavy lines, like flowing water.
steps: Rivers are usually shown with blue wavy lines, like flowing water.
Answer: a river
quiz.mistake: Does not link blue with water on maps

quiz.q: How is a map different from the real place?
options: It can only show one house
quiz.explain: A map is a small drawing, so a whole town can fit on one page.
steps: A map is a small drawing of a real place.
A whole town can fit on one page.
Answer: It is much smaller

learn.hook: Rub a leaf, sniff a flower, touch the bark. Plants are full of surprises!
points: Trees are tall plants with one thick, hard, woody stem called a trunk, like neem, mango and banyan.

Herbs are small plants with soft green stems, like coriander (dhania), mint (pudina) and wheat.
Climbers have weak stems and climb up with support, like the money plant and the pea plant. Creepers spread on the ground, like pumpkin and watermelon.

topics.title: Biodiversity: so many kinds of life

learn.hook: From tiny ants to giant elephants, India is home to an amazing variety of life!
points: Biodiversity means the great variety of plants and animals found in a place.
Different animals and plants live in different places: forests, deserts, rivers, seas and mountains.
Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros. Gir in Gujarat is the home of Asiatic lions.
The Sundarbans in West Bengal have mangrove forests and the Royal Bengal tiger. Snow leopards live high in the Himalayas.
The tiger is India's national animal, the peacock is our national bird and the lotus is our national flower.

example.q: Think it through: A forest has many kinds of trees, birds, insects and animals. Why is this good?
steps: Each living thing has a job in nature.
Bees help flowers, birds spread seeds, and trees give shelter.
If many kinds live together, nature stays balanced and healthy.
example.answer: A forest with high biodiversity stays healthy because living things help each other.

learn.hook: Honey, bamboo, fruits and fresh air: a forest is like a giant free gift shop!
points: A forest is a large area thickly covered with trees, bushes and other plants. Many animals live there.
Forests give us wood, bamboo, fruits, honey, gum and medicinal plants.
Many communities live in and near forests. They collect forest things carefully and take only what they need.
Leaves of the sal tree are stitched into plates and bowls called pattal and dona.
Tree roots hold the soil in place, and forests help keep the air clean and cool.

learn.hook: Would you hug a tree to protect it? Some brave people did just that!
points: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan follows rules that say green trees must not be cut and animals must be protected.
In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi of Khejarli village in Rajasthan hugged khejri trees to stop them from being cut. Many villagers joined her.
Bishnois also protect animals like the blackbuck and the chinkara.
In the 1970s, villagers in the hills of Uttarakhand, many of them women, hugged trees to stop them from being cut. This was called the Chipko movement.
'Chipko' means 'to stick' or 'to hug'. Gaura Devi led the women of Reni village in this movement in 1974.

example.q: Think it through: Why did the villagers in the Chipko movement hug the trees?
steps: Workers had come to cut down the trees.
The trees gave the villagers firewood and fodder, and held the soil on the slopes.
By hugging the trees, the villagers stood between the workers and the trees.
example.answer: To stop the trees from being cut, because the forest was important for their lives.

learn.hook: One man planted a whole forest by himself! You can start with one seed.
points: Some communities keep patches of forest as sacred groves. No one cuts trees there, so plants and animals stay safe.

Jadav Payeng of Assam planted trees on a sandy island in the Brahmaputra for many years. It grew into a big forest called the Molai forest.

learn.hook: How can a small child lift a big friend on a seesaw? The secret is a simple machine!
points: A simple machine is a tool that makes work easier. It helps us lift, move or cut things with less effort.
A lever is a strong bar that turns on a fixed point called the fulcrum. A seesaw, a hand pump handle and a bottle opener are levers.
A pair of scissors is made of two levers joined at a point.
A wheel and axle is a wheel fixed to a rod. Bicycle wheels and bullock cart wheels help us move loads easily.
A pulley is a wheel with a groove for a rope. Pulling the rope down lifts a load up, like a bucket from a well or a flag up a pole.

example.q: Think it through: Why is it easier to raise the flag on Independence Day using a pulley at the top of the pole?
steps: The flag must go up a tall pole.
Climbing the pole would be hard and unsafe.
With a pulley, we pull the rope down from the ground.
The pulley turns that pull into an upward lift.
example.answer: The pulley lets us pull down from the ground to send the flag up, which is easier and safer.

learn.hook: Why do workers roll heavy drums up a plank instead of lifting them? Let us find out!
points: A ramp, or inclined plane, is a sloping surface. It makes it easier to move heavy things up or down.

A wedge is thick at one end and thin or sharp at the other. It is used to cut or split things, like a knife or an axe.
A screw is a rod with a groove that winds around it. The lid of a jar works like a screw.
Using a ramp, we push with less effort, but we move the load over a longer distance.

points: A raw material is the basic thing from which something new is made.

Many raw materials come from plants: cotton, wood, bamboo, sugarcane and jute.
Some come from animals, like milk, wool and silk. Others come from the earth, like clay, sand and iron.
Glass is made from sand, paper from wood or bamboo pulp, and jaggery (gur) from sugarcane juice.

learn.hook: A potter's wheel spins, wet clay rises, and a pot is born! Every product goes through steps.

Clay to pot: clay is mixed with water and kneaded, shaped on a potter's wheel, dried in the sun and then baked in a hot kiln to make it strong.
Wheat to roti: wheat is harvested, the grains are separated, ground into atta, kneaded into dough, rolled and cooked.
If the steps are done in the wrong order, the product will not come out right.

learn.hook: Hot sand, very little rain and camels walking slowly: welcome to the Thar Desert!

topics.title: The sun, the moon and the stars

learn.hook: Look up! By day the sun shines, and at night the moon and thousands of stars twinkle.
points: The sun is a star. It is the star nearest to the Earth, and it gives us light and heat.
The sun looks small only because it is very far away. It is much, much bigger than the Earth.
The moon goes around the Earth. It has no light of its own. It shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces back to us.

Stars are huge, hot balls of glowing gas. They look tiny because they are very, very far away. Groups of stars that make patterns are called constellations. The Saptarishi is a famous pattern of seven bright stars.
Never look straight at the sun, not even with sunglasses. It can badly hurt your eyes.

learn.hook: Some nights the moon is a thin smile, some nights a full round plate. Is it really changing shape?
points: The moon does not really change its shape. Half of it is always lit by the sun.
As the moon goes around the Earth, we see different amounts of its lit part. These changing shapes are called phases of the moon.
On the new moon night (Amavasya), we cannot see the moon. On the full moon night (Purnima), we see a full round moon.
After the new moon, the lit part grows night by night: crescent, half moon, then full moon. After the full moon, it shrinks again.
From one full moon to the next takes about 29 and a half days, nearly a month.
